Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

RK2・RK4は次数、SSPは安定性の継承を表し、異なる問いに答えます。RK系譜ノートでは、9つの陽解法の全段階係数、非線形予測値、線形安定領域、実測収束次数を比べます。

## Runge–Kutta法：段数、次数、安定性、SSP — 1ステップと複数の右辺評価# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/runge-kutta/#one-step-several-right-hand-side-evaluations
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

y′=f(t,y)の陽的s段RK法は、
Y_i=y_n+h\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}k_j,\qquad
k_i=f(t_n+c_i h,Y_i),\qquad
y_{n+1}=y_n+h\sum_{i=1}^s b_i k_i,
\qquad c_i=\sum_{j<i}a_{ij}.
です。Butcher表はc、A、bを係数図にまとめます。段数sは本実装の右辺評価回数です。次数pは、必要な滑らかさ・安定性・固定区間の仮定で大域誤差O(h^p)を意味します。段階予測値Y_iは一般に途中時刻の高精度解ではありません。段階時刻は逆戻りする場合があり、SSPRK(4,3)はc=(0,1/2,1,1/2)で評価します。時間依存外力・境界値には、次の時刻順の割合ではなく正しいc_iを使います。

## Runge–Kutta法：段数、次数、安定性、SSP — RK2はひとつの族# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/runge-kutta/#rk2-is-a-family
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

2段・2次の族を、
k_1=f(t_n,y_n),\quad
k_2=f(t_n+\alpha h,y_n+\alpha h k_1),\quad
y_{n+1}=y_n+h\left[\left(1-\frac1{2\alpha}\right)k_1+
\frac1{2\alpha}k_2\right].
と書けます。Heun／陽的台形則はalpha=1、陽的中点は1/2、Ralstonは2/3です。HeunはSSPRK(2,2)でもあります。ここでの完全な非線形法のSSP係数は、それぞれ1、0、1/2で、全Butcher表の絶対単調性不等式から確認します。
3法ともスカラー線形安定性多項式は、
R(z)=1+z+\tfrac12 z^2,\qquad z=h\lambda.
です。そのため、厳密算術ではy′=lambda yの軌道は同じですが、非線形段階や誤差は一致するとは限りません。ノートでは厳密解1/(1+t)を持つy′=−y²、y(0)=1も計算し、振動子だけでは見分けられない違いを示します。ひとつの問題から普遍的に最良のRK2は決められません。

## Runge–Kutta法：段数、次数、安定性、SSP — RK3、古典的RK4、SSPの段数# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/runge-kutta/#rk3-classical-rk4-and-ssp-stage-counts
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

実装した3次群は、Kuttaの古典的3段、SSPRK(3,3)、SSPRK(4,3)です。前二者はR(z)=1+z+z²/2+z³/6を共有しますが、非線形SSP係数は0と1です。SSPRK(4,3)は4回目の右辺評価を使い、C=2、追加項z⁴/48を持ちます。4段だから4次になるわけではありません。
古典的4段RK4の重みは(1/6,1/3,1/3,1/6)です。安定性多項式はz⁴/24を加え、4次精度です。一般の非線形SSP係数はゼロです。すべてのRK4計算が振動するのではなく、一般的な前進EulerからのSSP継承保証が使えないという意味です。NumipediaのRK4記録に係数表とスカラー安定性があります。
比較用にSpiteri–Ruuthの5段4次SSP法SSPRK(5,4)も実装します。全係数はGottlieb–Ketcheson–Shu総説第3.1節です。小数Shu–Osher形式をButcher表へ変換し、y_nからの増分で表現することで丸めたアフィン重みのずれを避けます。厳密有理係数とはせず、控えめな丸め限界C=1.508を使い、与えた精度で次数条件と非線形収束を検査します。
一般の非線形SSP係数が正の標準陽的RK法では次数は最大4です。4段4次の陽解法はC>0を持てないため、4次SSPには追加段が必要です。SSPRK(5,4)は一例で、すべての5段4次法がSSPなのではありません。Spiteri–Ruuth（2002）、Gottlieb–Ketcheson–Shu（2009）。

## Runge–Kutta法：段数、次数、安定性、SSP — SSPが保存するもの# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/runge-kutta/#what-ssp-preserves
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

特定の半離散空間演算子Lが、h≤h_FEで前進Eulerに対して凸安定性を満たすとします。係数CのSSP法は、
h\le C h_{\rm FE}.
でそれを継承します。前提は全変動、ノルム、許容凸集合などですが、実際の演算子と段階処理が条件を満たす必要があります。SSPはTVD空間離散化を生み出したり、不適切な境界を直したり、欠けたEuler正値状態を補ったりはしません。Gottlieb–Shu–Tadmor（2001）の総説がこの視点を説明します。勾配制限と正値再構成の別の要件と比較してください。
表記は**SSPRK(s,p)**で、先が段数、後が次数です。初版ではHeun／SSPRK(2,2)はC=1、SSPRK(3,3)は1、SSPRK(4,3)は2、SSPRK(5,4)は丸め限界1.508です。右辺評価あたりのSSP刻み限界C/sは参考になりますが、実行時間の順位ではありません。メモリー転送、記憶量、空間精度、他の安定制約が実際のコストを左右します。

## Runge–Kutta法：段数、次数、安定性、SSP — 線形安定性は別の図# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/runge-kutta/#linear-stability-is-a-separate-picture
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

y′=lambda yでは、1ステップの倍率は、
R(z)=1+z\,b^T(I-zA)^{-1}{\bf1}.
です。|R(z)|≤1がスカラー絶対安定領域です。Re(z)∈[−6,2]、Im(z)∈[−4,4]の401×401格子で境界を標本化し、曲線は近似等高線であって厳密な境界位置ではありません。正規な線形空間演算子なら固有値からRの評価位置を考えられますが、非正規演算子の一時的増大は固有値だけでは見落とします。
無減衰振動子でRK2には虚軸上のゼロでない安定区間がなく、SSPRK(3,3)と古典的RK4にはあります。これはスカラー線形問題の性質で、前進Euler自身もこの振動子でゼロでない安定刻みを持たないため、HeunのSSP性とは矛盾しません。

## Runge–Kutta法：段数、次数、安定性、SSP — 時間積分の他の分岐# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/runge-kutta/#other-branches-of-the-time-integration-family
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

Dormand–Prince 5(4)などの埋込みRK対は、2つの次数で誤差と刻みを推定します。この括弧は埋込み次数で、SSPRK(s,p)の段数・次数とは違います。初版では埋込み誤差推定、適応制御、連続出力、FSAL最適化は実行しません。
低記憶RKは段階計算を組み替えて配列を減らしますが、自動的にSSPにはなりません。陰的RKには中点、Gauss／Radau／SDIRKなどがあり、非線形求解と独自の安定性を持ちます。IMEX対は陽的・陰的演算子を分けます。既存のスカラー線形後退Euler・陰的中点の実演を除き、ここでは読書の背景です。下の汎用rk_stepは9つの陽的Butcher表だけに対応します。leapfrogは多段階漸化式、力学Verletとシンプレクティック写像はさらに別の分岐です。

## Runge–Kutta法：段数、次数、安定性、SSP — 再現と検証# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/runge-kutta/#reproduction-and-verification
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

from numart.runge_kutta import rk_step, nonlinear_trajectory
value, stages = rk_step(lambda t, y: -y*y, 0., 1., 0.5,
 method="ssprk43", return_stages=True)
t, y = nonlinear_trajectory("ssprk54", steps=40)
python scripts/build_runge_kutta.py
python scripts/sync_web_content.py
JSONには全係数表、等高線、27個の1ステップ段階例（h=0.25、0.5、1）、9つの細分化（N=10、20、40、80、T=1）、ソースハッシュを記録します。誤差は厳密な非線形解を使い、段階は実際の右辺評価です。テストでは4次までの全次数条件、非線形製造時間依存方程式、複素線形安定係数、指定Cでの全係数表SSP不等式、継承した刻み制約でのスカラーMUSCL保存／TVDを確認します。既存Euler／WENOがRK選択可能や完全正値性保存になるわけではありません。

## 波追跡PPM、AUSM系と曲面前方の衝撃波 — 直接Euler型PPMと独立したスイッチ# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/shock-expansion/#direct-eulerian-ppm-and-independent-switches
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

numart.ppm_tracedは保存変数セル平均から密度・速度・圧力の基本変数を再構成します。MC制限した放物線補間、任意の密度接触面急峻化、衝撃波平坦化、成分ごとの放物線単調性制約を使います。セル平均保存量は共有面流束で更新します。平均保存変数から作る基本変数分布は2次精度の表現であり、基本変数の厳密な平均ではありません。
セル内座標xi∈[0,1]では、各成分の分布は次式です。
q(\xi)=q_L+\xi[\Delta q+q_6(1-\xi)],\qquad
\Delta q=q_R-q_L,\qquad q_6=6q_i-3(q_L+q_R).
各端から幅sigmaの領域にわたる平均を取ります。
I_R(\sigma)=q_R-\frac{\sigma}{2}\left[\Delta q-\left(1-\frac{2\sigma}{3}\right)q_6\right],\qquad
I_L(\sigma)=q_L+\frac{\sigma}{2}\left[\Delta q+\left(1-\frac{2\sigma}{3}\right)q_6\right].
特性速度はu−c、u、u+cです。面に到達する各波族にsigma=|lambda| dt/dxを使います。最速の到達波の領域平均を出発点として、セル状態に固定した基本変数の固有ベクトルを使い、他の到達波成分を補正します。これらは1回の保存更新に用いる時間平均Riemann入力です。この予測の外側にさらにSSPRK3を適用すると別の方法になります。既定値はHLLCとCFL 0.4です。
確認したColella–Woodward著者プレプリントの直接Euler型特性領域の考え方に従い、1984年論文を原典とします。Cholla著者原稿の付録Aも手順の照合に使いました。独立した実装であり、全プロダクションコードの選択肢、多次元CTU、人工粘性、Lagrange発展、remapを再現するものではありません。Cholla付録に表示された一部の符号・添字は、説明されている隣接セル構成と整合しないため、ここに示す式と実行検証で本変種を定義します。

## 波追跡PPM、AUSM系と曲面前方の衝撃波 — 接触面急峻化と衝撃波平坦化# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/shock-expansion/#contact-steepening-and-shock-flattening
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

急峻化は密度の端値だけを変えます。D2_i=(rho_(i+1)−2rho_i+rho_(i−1))/6とし、D2_(i−1) D2_(i+1)<0、相対密度差が0.01より大きいこと、相対圧力差が相対密度差の0.1 gamma倍より小さいことを要求します。そのとき、
\widetilde\eta_i=-\frac{D^2_{i+1}-D^2_{i-1}}{\rho_{i+1}-\rho_{i-1}},\qquad
\eta_i=\operatorname{clip}\!\left(20(\widetilde\eta_i-0.05),0,1\right).
左端をrho_(i−1)+delta_rho_(i−1)/2、右端をrho_(i+1)−delta_rho_(i+1)/2に近づけます。delta_rhoは隣接セルのMC制限勾配です。接触面の拡散を抑えますが、解像されていない滑らかな密度遷移も急にする場合があります。普遍的な精度改善とは扱いません。
平坦化はS_i=(p_(i+1)−p_(i−1))/(p_(i+2)−p_(i−2))を使います。予備係数clip(10(S_i−0.75),0,1)は、相対圧力差が1/3以上で、速度差が圧縮的な場所だけで有効にします。対象セルと低圧側隣接セルの大きい係数を採用し、単調性制約の前に、すべての基本変数の端値をセル値へ近づけます。係数1では空間変動が消え、0では変更しません。
再構成入力が密度・圧力の1e−12という閾値を満たさない場合、変更しないセル平均を中心に、保存変数の共通アフィンスケーリングを適用します。更新後が非物理的なら時間刻みを半分にして最大14回試行します。これらは対策であり、完全離散化の正値性の証明ではありません。停止時は最後の許容状態と実際の時刻を残します。状態の切り詰め、非表示の流束切替、誤った最終時刻ラベルは使いません。
4つのスイッチ組合せは、同じ流束・名目CFL・更新法を使います。N=200で接触面が1周期移動する問題では、急峻化が密度誤差を減らし、圧力と速度は丸め誤差程度で一定です。滑らかなエントロピー波のN=32,64,128では、波追跡を含む全手法がほぼ2次収束します。時間3次・4次という主張ではありません。

## 波追跡PPM、AUSM系と曲面前方の衝撃波 — 条件を明示したAUSM+とAUSM+-up# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/shock-expansion/#ausm-and-ausm-up-with-stated-controls
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

従来の算術平均音速AUSMは別に維持します。新しい流束は4次Mach分割と5次圧力分割を使います。|M|<1で、
\mathcal M_4^\pm(M)=\pm\left[\frac{(M\pm1)^2}{4}+\frac{(M^2-1)^2}{8}\right],\qquad
\mathcal P_5^\pm(M)=\frac{(M\pm1)^2(2\mp M)}4\pm\alpha M(M^2-1)^2.
その外では符号に応じた風上Mach・圧力分率を使います。両変種とも、2006年の定式化で用いられる方向別の臨界エンタルピー音速を採用します。
a_{*,k}^2=\frac{2(\gamma-1)}{\gamma+1}H_k,\qquad
a_f=\min\left(\frac{a_{*,L}^2}{\max(a_{*,L},u_L)},
\frac{a_{*,R}^2}{\max(a_{*,R},-u_R)}\right).
表示する**AUSM+**はalpha=3/16で、圧力・速度拡散項を使いません。この定式化の基本形を明示したもので、1996年のすべての界面音速の選択肢を再現する主張ではありません。AUSM+-upではKp=0.25、Ku=0.75、sigma=1、参照Mach数の下限を0.1とします。
\overline M^2=\frac{M_L^2+M_R^2}{2},\quad
M_0=\sqrt{\min(1,\max(\overline M^2,M_{\rm ref}^2))},\quad
f_a=M_0(2-M_0),\quad\alpha=\frac{3}{16}(5f_a^2-4).
圧力拡散を界面Mach数に、速度拡散を界面圧力に加えます。
M_p=-\frac{K_p}{f_a}\max(1-\overline M^2,0)
\frac{p_R-p_L}{\overline\rho a_f^2},\qquad
p_u=-K_u f_a\mathcal P_5^+(M_L)\mathcal P_5^-(M_R)
(\rho_L+\rho_R)a_f(u_R-u_L).
得られた質量流束の符号で密度・速度・全エンタルピーを風上化し、法線運動量には界面圧力を加えます。一様流、両方向の超音速風上化、接触面、定常垂直衝撃波、音速分岐の接続、向き反転時の保存性、回転共変性を検証します。
原典はLiou（1996）とLiou（2006）です。音速と拡散項の定義はSU2公式実装と照合しました。Pythonは独立実装で、陰的Jacobianや時間前処理は提供しません。
低Machグラフは、小さな固定圧力差に対し下限を0.01、0.1、1と変えます。これは流束の感度であり、低Mach渦・境界層・漸近保存的PDE手法の検証ではありません。下限値と時間刻み制限も数値的方法の一部です。

## 波追跡PPM、AUSM系と曲面前方の衝撃波 — 条件を揃えた1次元問題と停止例# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/shock-expansion/#matched-one-dimensional-problems-and-a-recorded-failure
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

新しい1次元計算は波追跡PPMとCFL 0.4を使います。流束比較では接触面急峻化を無効、衝撃波平坦化を有効に固定し、HLLC、旧AUSM、AUSM+、AUSM+-upを切り替えます。独立した適応CFL計算であり、ステップ数や費用を揃えた比較ではありません。
Sod N=200、移動接触面N=200、Shu–Osher N=240、強い圧力跳躍N=200を使います。最初の3つは以前の比較と同じ定義です。最後は基本変数が左(1,0,1000)、右(1,0,0.01)、gamma=1.4、区間[0,1]、x=0.5の跳び、両端外挿、t=0.01です。この時刻まで波は境界に到達しません。
Sodと強圧力差の密度誤差は、保存変数Riemann状態を波面で分割した24点・48点求積を使います。接触面は1周期で初期セル平均へ戻ります。Shu–Osherは従来の内部的な特性FD WENO-Z N=960参照計算を使います。数値参照解であり厳密解ではないため、厳密誤差は報告しません。参照点値と平均保存変数の基本変数は、異なる規約です。
この強圧力差のAUSM+設定では、t=0.01に達する前に許容状態を得る再試行を使い切ります。表に失敗と実際の停止時刻を表示し、最終時刻の曲線から除外します。ダウンロードには最後の許容保存状態と理由を残します。流束・再構成対策・名目CFLだけでは更新の正値性が保証されない例です。完了した他の計算にも再試行があるため、回数を確認してください。

## 波追跡PPM、AUSM系と曲面前方の衝撃波 — 円柱前面に沿う保存的メッシュ# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/shock-expansion/#a-conservative-mesh-around-the-cylinder-nose
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

単位半径円柱の上流側半分だけを扱います。r∈[1,4]、theta∈[pi/2,3pi/2]、流れは正のx方向です。直線辺を持つ環状四角形が、円柱の多角形近似に沿います。格子は24×48と48×96の2水準です。半径と角度は等間隔ですが、物理的なセルは正方形ではありません。
Cartesian保存変数を、共有する面長と面法線流束で更新します。多角形面積、半径方向弦面の法線、角方向面の法線は、丸め誤差程度で幾何学的な閉鎖条件を満たします。曲線座標の運動量ソース項は不要です。壁を無効にした一様流保存、壁法線運動量の反射、壁の質量・エネルギー流束ゼロ、全領域流束収支を検証します。
rho_inf=1.4、p_inf=1、u_inf=6、v_inf=0、gamma=1.4で、音速1・Mach 6です。内壁は非粘性slip、外周は一様流固定、角方向の両出口は外挿です。初期一様流に、必要に応じ次の密度摂動を加えます。
\rho(r,\theta)=\rho_\infty\left[1+\epsilon
e^{-((r-1.5)/0.3)^2}\sin\bigl(12(\theta-\pi)\bigr)\right],\qquad
\epsilon\in\{0,10^{-4}\}.
初期速度と圧力は変えません。メッシュや衝撃波位置を動かす摂動ではなく、密度の角方向モードです。細分化しても角波長は一定です。対照計算と摂動計算には、空間1次の幾何学的有限体積法、SSPRK2、CFL 0.4、終了時刻2を使います。CFLは全セル面のスペクトル半径の和から定め、1次元のCFL規則と数値的に同一ではありません。5流束×2格子×2摂動振幅で計20計算です。

## 波追跡PPM、AUSM系と曲面前方の衝撃波 — HLLEとRoeの方向分解による合成# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/shock-expansion/#directional-hlle-and-roe-composition
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

面法線nに対して、速度差の方向にn1、その直交方向にn2を選びます。alpha_k=n dot n_kが非負になるよう符号を揃えます。この無次元設定で速度差が1e−10以下なら、n1を面接線、n2を面法線とします。
\widehat{\boldsymbol F}(\boldsymbol n)=
\alpha_1\widehat{\boldsymbol F}_{\rm HLLE}(\boldsymbol n_1)+
\alpha_2\widehat{\boldsymbol F}_{\rm Roe}(\boldsymbol n_2),\qquad
\boldsymbol n=\alpha_1\boldsymbol n_1+\alpha_2\boldsymbol n_2.
同じ左右の物理状態を各局所座標系に回転し、運動量流束をCartesian座標へ戻してから合成します。法線方向の速度差ではHLLE、純粋な接線せん断では面法線方向のRoeが選ばれます。物理Euler流束は法線に線形なので、一様状態の整合性を保ちます。流束反転の保存性と回転検証も通過します。
Nishikawa・Kitamura（2008）を着想源とした、定義を明示したrotated-hybridの実験です。従来の圧力センサーRoe/HLLE混合とは異なり、原論文の最適化されたRotated-RHLL散逸式を再現したという主張でもありません。微小速度差時の切替と次元を持つ許容値は、明示した実装上の選択です。

## 波追跡PPM、AUSM系と曲面前方の衝撃波 — 前面計算から分かること# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/shock-expansion/#what-the-forebody-results-establish
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

5流束は音響エントロピー平滑化したRoe、Einfeldt型HLLE、AUSM+、AUSM+-up、方向分解HLLE/Roeです。各画像の5つの場は共通の色範囲です。slip壁圧力係数は実際の壁法線運動量流束を使い、よどみ点に最も近い2セルから先端圧力を報告します。
垂直衝撃波の跳躍と、その後の等エントロピー減速から、非粘性中心流線のよどみ圧参照値p0,2=46.8152057161を得ます。これはスカラーの流線参照値であり、弓形衝撃波全体の厳密場ではありません。境界層と後流は含みません。先端圧力、反射対称性の欠損、残る規格化更新率、正値性、積分保存残差を保存します。
細格子・摂動ありのRoeでは密度の反射対称性欠損が大きくなり、先端圧力は約25.0へ低下します。細格子HLLEは約47.38、粗格子は約48.81です。方向分解法とAUSM系にも、それぞれ異なる格子・摂動への応答があります。特に方向分解法は摂動なしの対照計算でも丸め誤差を増幅し得ます。非線形な方向選択では、対称に見える初期状態が厳密な離散対称性を保証しません。見栄えのよい1枚だけでなく、対照計算と履歴の両方を見てください。
これらは発展中の計算の終了時刻スナップショットです。更新率がゼロではなく、2格子だけなので、収束した定常解、漸近収束次数、普遍的なカーバンクル非発生を認定しません。長時間・時間刻みの検証、別Mach数、回転格子、外部コードとの照合、他のrotated-hybrid変種は残る検証です。円柱全体の粘性抗力・揚力・渦放出・Strouhal数は別課題です。

Coverage: reading

MPLCONFIGDIR=.mplconfig python scripts/build_shock_expansion.pyを実行します。前面計算のキャッシュは、数値ソースのハッシュと全設定が一致した場合だけ再利用します。条件・診断・ソースハッシュと保存状態・格子頂点・面積をダウンロードできます。停止した1次元計算には実際の時刻と最後の許容状態を含めます。要求最終時刻へ到達したものとして比較してはいけません。すべてのPNGと圧縮配列のハッシュも記録します。

Source note: 英語原文が更新されています。この日本語訳は旧版に対応します。

ロジスティック個体群増殖（Logistic population growth） — 文献解説のみ。 The linked original is the later 1847 memoir; the 1838 note itself was not audited. The differential equation is not the discrete logistic map.
Michaelis–Mentenと完全酵素反応系（Michaelis–Menten and full enzyme kinetics） — 文献解説のみ。 The 1913 rapid-equilibrium interpretation and the 1925 quasi-steady-state derivation must remain distinct.
Lotka–Volterra捕食・被食（Lotka–Volterra predator–prey） — 文献解説のみ。
McKendrick年齢構造個体群（McKendrick age-structured population） — 文献解説のみ。 This is the classical age-transport form; the later von Foerster lineage is acknowledged without treating its date as the first appearance.
SIR・SEIR区画モデル（SIR and SEIR compartment models） — 文献解説のみ。 The original general epidemic framework is broader than this SIR specialization. Population-count and fraction conventions give different β definitions.
Fisher–KPP侵入前線（Fisher–KPP invasion front） — 文献解説のみ。 Fisher–KPP is a conventional family name; the independent KPP 1937 original remains an archival follow-up. The exact special speed is not the minimal speed.
Monod増殖とケモスタット（Monod growth and chemostat） — 文献解説のみ。 This writes one constant-yield extension of saturation growth, not a universal metabolic model.

## 収録範囲と数え方 — 生物モデル調査# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/site-coverage/#biological-model-survey
Coverage: reading
Source note: 英語原文が更新されています。この日本語訳は旧版に対応します。

Hodgkin–Huxley膜動態（Hodgkin–Huxley membrane dynamics） — 文献解説のみ。 The original squid-axon model is not a calibrated human cardiac model. No single rate parameter set is selected by this survey.
Turing反応拡散の枠組み（Turing reaction–diffusion framework） — 文献解説のみ。 A spot image or unequal diffusion coefficients alone do not establish a Turing mechanism. Boundary conditions determine the available modes.
FitzHugh–Nagumoの興奮と回復（FitzHugh–Nagumo excitation and recovery） — 文献解説のみ。 This is a common normalized variant; cubic coefficients, recovery signs and nondimensionalization differ between formulations.
Keller–Segel走化性（Keller–Segel chemotaxis） — 文献解説のみ。 This is a common two-field reduction of a more detailed original formulation. Blowup thresholds depend on dimension, domain, boundary and chemical dynamics.
Gierer–Meinhardt活性化・抑制（Gierer–Meinhardt activator–inhibitor） — 文献解説のみ。 Source densities, saturation and baseline production vary across the model family. This simplified formula is not a verbatim transcription of every original variant.
流体・弾性構造と埋め込み境界（Fluid–elastic structure and immersed boundaries） — 文献解説のみ。 Immersed boundary is a numerical coupling method, not itself a closed biological constitutive equation. The existing periodic MAC solver does not implement this coupling.

## 収録範囲と数え方 — 生物モデル調査# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/site-coverage/#biological-model-survey
Coverage: reading
Source note: 英語原文が更新されています。この日本語訳は旧版に対応します。

化学マスター方程式とGillespie SSA（Chemical master equation and Gillespie SSA） — 文献解説のみ。 The 1977 paper is a foundational SSA reference, not a priority claim for all master equations. SSA is a solver; the reaction network is the model. A seed documents a trajectory, not an ensemble validation.
Mackey–Glass遅延生理フィードバック（Mackey–Glass delayed physiological feedback） — 文献解説のみ。 A scalar initial value alone is insufficient. The delayed ODE is distinct from a spatial reaction–diffusion model.
レプリケータ進化ゲーム動態（Replicator evolutionary game dynamics） — 文献解説のみ。 No universal Lyapunov function or equivalence of fixed point and evolutionarily stable strategy is assumed.
Schnakenberg反応拡散（Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion） — 文献解説のみ。 A mathematical chemical pattern model; matching a visual biological pattern does not calibrate it to a tissue.
Shigesada–Kawasaki–Teramoto交差拡散（Shigesada–Kawasaki–Teramoto cross-diffusion） — 文献解説のみ。 The displayed homogeneous-environment reduction omits the original environmental-potential terms. It is not equivalent to two independent scalar diffusion equations.
Gray–Scott空間自己触媒反応（Gray–Scott spatial autocatalysis） — 文献解説のみ。 1983 is the well-mixed CSTR source; Pearson 1993 is the spatial pattern reference. Spot division does not by itself demonstrate cell division or a linear Turing instability.

## 収録範囲と数え方 — 論文数と全資料数の区別# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/site-coverage/#papers-versus-all-sources
Coverage: reading
Source note: 英語原文が更新されています。この日本語訳は旧版に対応します。

論文数は学術誌論文と会議論文です。総説、翻訳、採録済みであることを明記した論文も含みます。全参考資料は、それに書籍、章、技術資料、文書、個別に識別したプレプリント等を加えた、重複を除く出版物の数です。
137件：学術誌論文（総説・翻訳・採録済み論文を含む）
3件：会議論文
22件：書籍
2件：書籍の章
3件：技術・教育レポート
10件：その他の資料・文書・プレプリント
Cockburn–Shu 1989の重複書誌を統合し、Burgers 1948を書籍の章に分類しました。以前の146レコードには重複があり、その後の出典追加も現在の重複を除く総数に反映しています。原著と別途出版された翻訳は異なる出版物です。すべての全文を確認済みとは主張せず、確認状態を各出典注記に残します。

集計一覧と出典ハッシュをダウンロード。参考文献、方程式ギャラリー、生物モデル、実装ロードマップも参照できます。

## 疎行列・非線形方程式系：真の残差を測る — 1986〜1992年：非対称Krylov法# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/sparse-nonlinear/#19861992-nonsymmetric-krylov-methods
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

Saad–Schultz（1986）がGMRES、van der Vorst（1992）がBiCGSTABを導入します。本実装のGMRESはArnoldi再直交化と小さなHessenberg最小二乗問題を使い、指定した内部反復回数で再始動します。BiCGSTABは破綻を明示し、残差は単調に減るとは限りません。
両実装は固定した右前処理を適用します。
A M^{-1} z=b,\qquad x=M^{-1}z,
\qquad \|b-Ax\|_2\leq\max(\mathrm{atol},\mathrm{rtol}\|b\|_2).
停止判定の履歴では真の残差を再計算します。Jacobiは対角スケーリングです。ILU(0)は与えた非ゼロ構造だけを保ち、追加のフィル、ピボット選択、並べ替えを行いません。非常に小さなピボットでは明示的に失敗します。実用的な頑健な疎行列分解を置き換えるものではありません。

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/sparse-nonlinear/#newton-and-conditioning
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

Newton法はJ(x)δ=−F(x)を解き、残差に対するArmijo減少条件を満たすよう後退探索でステップ長を選びます。Newton–Krylovの例はJを組み立ててGMRESを使い、行列不要方式ではありません。Bratu方程式を2つの空間解像度で解析解と比較し、内部求解の失敗も検査します。
残差が小さくても、解誤差が小さいとは限りません。
\frac{\|x-\hat x\|}{\|x\|}
\leq \kappa(A)\frac{\|b-A\hat x\|}{\|b\|}.
条件数、固有値分布、非正規性は異なる性質を表します。条件数が小さいことだけで再始動GMRESの優劣は決められません。CGには引き続き対称正定値演算子と適切な対称正定値前処理が必要で、一般のILU(0)がその条件を満たすとはしていません。
非対称の例は、ゼロDirichlet条件での1次風上移流と中心差分拡散です。1反復あたりの計算量が異なるため、図では実行時間の順位を付けません。データとソースハッシュ、FEMの組立て、陰的ODE段階も参照してください。

## 差分、CFL条件、von Neumann解析、Laxの定理 — 差分、CFL条件、von Neumann解析、Laxの定理 [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stability/
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

安定性実験室と実験ガイドで、以下の式をブラウザー内の計算と結び付けて確かめられます。

## 差分、CFL条件、von Neumann解析、Laxの定理 — 空間と時間の離散化を別々に選ぶ# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stability/#choose-space-and-time-discretizations-separately
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

前進差分（forward difference）、後退差分（backward difference）、中心差分（centered difference）は、それぞれ次のように定義します。
D_+u_j=\frac{u_{j+1}-u_j}{h},\qquad
D_-u_j=\frac{u_j-u_{j-1}}h,\qquad
D_0u_j=\frac{u_{j+1}-u_{j-1}}{2h}.
滑らかな関数に対して、前二者は1次、中心差分は2次精度です。numart.advection.finite_differenceで比較できます。線形移流u_t+a u_x=0の風上差分（upwind difference）は情報の伝播方向に従い、a>0では後退差分、a<0では前進差分を使います。したがって、前進差分と風上差分は同じ意味ではありません。
時間方向の前進Euler法はu^{n+1}=u^n+Δt L_h u^n、後退Euler法はu^{n+1}=u^n+Δt L_h u^{n+1}で、後者では方程式系を解きます。空間に後退差分を使うだけで陰解法になるわけではありません。

## 差分、CFL条件、von Neumann解析、Laxの定理 — CFL条件と数値的な依存領域# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stability/#cfl-can-the-stencil-reach-the-information-it-needs
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

定係数・周期移流を隣接格子点までの陽的差分で解く場合、依存領域の議論から|a|Δt/h ≤ 1が必要です。この定数は差分、Runge–Kutta法、DGの次数、次元によって変わります。陽的拡散にはΔt=O(h²)の制約が現れます。CFL条件は一般に安定性の必要条件であり、十分条件ではありません。Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy（1928）。
時間前進・空間中心差分（FTCS）の移流が反例です。Fourierモードu_j^n=G^n e^{ijθ}を代入すると、
G=1-i C\sin θ,\quad |G|^2=1+C^2\sin^2 θ,
\qquad C=a\Delta t/h.
となり、|C|<1でも増幅するモードがあります。通常のCFL数を固定した格子細分化に対して、この方式は不安定です。

## 差分、CFL条件、von Neumann解析、Laxの定理 — Lax–Friedrichs法とLax–Wendroff法# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stability/#laxfriedrichs-and-laxwendroff
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

古典的なLax–Friedrichs法は、
u_j^{n+1}=\tfrac12(u_{j+1}^n+u_{j-1}^n)
-\tfrac C2(u_{j+1}^n-u_{j-1}^n),\qquad
G=\cos θ-iC\sin θ.
です。|G|²=1-(1-C²)sin²θより、この周期線形移流問題では|C|≤1で安定です。古典的LFの数値粘性係数はh/Δtです。Rusanov流束は局所最大波速を使い、本実装のWENOは大域LF流束分割を使います。これらは異なる離散構成です。Lax（1954）。
Lax–Wendroff法は、
u_j^{n+1}=u_j^n-\tfrac C2(u_{j+1}^n-u_{j-1}^n)
+\tfrac{C^2}{2}(u_{j+1}^n-2u_j^n+u_{j-1}^n),
であり、増幅係数は、
G=1-iC\sin θ+C^2(\cos θ-1),\quad
|G|^2=1-4C^2(1-C^2)\sin^4(θ/2).
です。この問題での安定条件は同じく|C|≤1です。2次精度であること自体は、不連続近傍の振動を抑える保証にはなりません。Lax–Wendroff（1960）。
テストではamplificationによる解析的な増幅係数と、difference_stepによる実際のモード発展を比較します。図では小さなNyquist摂動を加え、C=0.8とC=1.1を比較しています。

## 差分、CFL条件、von Neumann解析、Laxの定理 — Lax–Richtmyerの同値定理# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stability/#the-laxrichtmyer-equivalence-theorem
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

適切なBanach空間上の適切に設定された線形初期値問題と、整合的な線形差分近似を考えます。固定した有限時間区間で離散発展演算子が一様有界であることを安定性とすると、安定性と収束性は同値です。Lax–Richtmyer（1956）の原論文。
誤差をe^{n+1}=S_h e^n+Δt τ^nと書けば、||S_h^m||≤M_Tから||e^n||≤M_T||e^0||+M_T T max||τ^k||を得ます。整合性により打切り誤差の項がゼロへ向かい、安定性から収束性を導く基本的な議論になります。逆向きには一様有界性の議論が必要です。
この定理から、非線形Euler、WENO、衝撃波、任意の境界処理の正しさを直接保証することはできません。ここでのFourier条件|G|≤1は、周期・定係数のスカラー問題に適用しています。境界、変係数、非正規行列、多段階法には追加の解析が必要です。

## 差分、CFL条件、von Neumann解析、Laxの定理 — 初版で用いる時間刻み# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stability/#time-steps-in-the-first-edition
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

Euler系・バロトロピック系：Δt=C h/max(|u|+c)、既定値C=0.3。
DG：Δt=C h/((2p+1)|a|)、既定値C=0.2。
2次元MHD：Δt=C/[max(s_x)/h+max(s_y)/h]、既定値C=0.3。
これらは選定した例で確認した控えめな設定です。すべての初期条件に対する厳密な非線形安定限界ではありません。
A安定性・L安定性とL1／L2／L∞誤差ノルムの定義と比較は、精度と安定性の共通ガイドを参照してください。

## 硬い方程式の積分：段階を解き、時間誤差を制御する — 硬い方程式の積分：段階を解き、時間誤差を制御する [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stiff-integration/
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

実装済み：後退Euler法、その初期化を使う固定刻みBDF2、2段階SDIRK2、1次IMEX Euler、ステップ倍分割による適応SDIRK2。すべての非線形段階に減衰Newton法を使い、失敗を明示します。

## 硬い方程式の積分：段階を解き、時間誤差を制御する — 陰的段階と安定性# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stiff-integration/#implicit-stages-and-stability
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

後退Euler法はy_new−y_old−h f(t_new,y_new)=0を解きます。BDF2は、
\frac{3y_{n+1}-4y_n+y_{n-1}}{2h}=f(t_{n+1},y_{n+1}).
を解きます。ここで使うL安定、2段階、2次精度の単一対角陰的公式の出典はAlexander（1977）です。
\gamma=1-1/\sqrt2,\qquad
A=\begin{pmatrix}\gamma&0\\1-\gamma&\gamma\end{pmatrix},
\quad b=(1-\gamma,\gamma),\quad c=(\gamma,1).
各対角段階は別々の非線形求解です。陰解法では陽解法の安定限界を超える刻みを使える場合がありますが、実用的な刻み幅は精度でも制限されます。収束したNewton残差が測るのは段階方程式であり、時間離散化誤差ではありません。

## 硬い方程式の積分：段階を解き、時間誤差を制御する — 適応刻みと陽陰分割# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/stiff-integration/#adaptive-and-split-steps
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

適応実装はSDIRK2の1全ステップと2半ステップを比べます。局所誤差推定は(y_half−y_full)/3で、atol+rtol max(|y_old|,|y_half|)で尺度化します。Richardson外挿はせず、2半ステップの値を採用し、指数−1/3でhを調整します。棄却試行と受理ステップを数え、試行上限に達するとエラーにします。
IMEX Eulerは一方を陽的、他方を陰的に評価します。この最小の1次分割は、Ascher–Ruuth–Spiteri（1997）の高次IMEX RK構成ではありません。陽的部分には独自の安定制約が残ります。可変刻みBDF、埋込みDIRK対、演算子分割は今後の拡張です。
硬いテストy′=−1000(y−cos t)−sin tは、y(0)=1のとき厳密解cos tを持ちます。計算記録は、実際の積分節点での最大誤差と適応ステップ数を残します。別のテストで、非線形・非自律ODEの次数と、硬い減衰モードの強い減衰を確認します。
外力付きの硬い問題の粗い刻み列は、一様な2次収束の範囲にはありません。BDF2の開始処理と硬い系の次数低下が、節点全体の最大誤差へ影響します。形式的な時間次数は、非線形・非硬性の次数テストで別に確認します。
A安定性・L安定性とL1／L2／L∞誤差ノルムは、精度と安定性の共通ガイドを参照してください。

## シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける — シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/symplectic/
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

シンプレクティック積分器は正準2形式を保ちながらHamilton系を進めます。多くの軌道・粒子積分の良い長時間挙動を支える写像の性質ですが、元のHamiltonianを一般に厳密保存するわけではありません。Hamilton写像ノートは2つの問いを計算例で分けます。

## シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける — 写像が保存するもの# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/symplectic/#what-the-map-preserves
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

状態z=(q,p)に対し、Hamilton方程式とシンプレクティック条件は、
\dot z=J\nabla H(z),\qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad D\Phi_h(z)^T J D\Phi_h(z)=J.
です。最後の恒等式は各数値ステップが正準変換であることを示します。1自由度ではdet(D Phi)=1と同値で、向き付き位相面積を保ちます。高次元で総体積だけを保つ条件は、それより弱いものです。
2形式の保存、Hの保存、時間対称性Phi_(−h)=Phi_h^(−1)を別々に検査します。シンプレクティックEulerはその違いの例で、一般に厳密エネルギー保存でも時間対称でもありません。

## シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける — Hamiltonianを分けて厳密な部分流を合成する# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/symplectic/#split-the-hamiltonian-compose-exact-subflows
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

単位質量の可分系H(q,p)=p²/2+V(q)では、2つの部分流はドリフトとキックです。
D_h(q,p)=(q+hp,p),\qquad K_h(q,p)=(q,p-h\nabla V(q)).
それぞれがシンプレクティックで、合成もそうなります。ノートにはkick–driftのシンプレクティックEulerと、対称2次のStörmer–Verlet、
p_{n+1/2}=p_n-\frac h2\nabla V(q_n),\quad
q_{n+1}=q_n+h p_{n+1/2},\quad
p_{n+1}=p_{n+1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(q_{n+1}).
があります。これは力学のleapfrog／速度Verletで、時間積分ノートの2ステップスカラー漸化式とは異なります。

## シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける — 合成で4次へ# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/symplectic/#fourth-order-by-composition
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

VerletステップをS2(h)とすると、4次合成の一例は、
S_4(h)=S_2(a h)\,S_2(b h)\,S_2(a h),\qquad
a=\frac1{2-2^{1/3}},\quad b=-\frac{2^{1/3}}{2-2^{1/3}}.
です。Yoshida（1990）は高次シンプレクティック合成を発展させます。bが負なので内部部分ステップは時間を逆行します。ここでの滑らかな保存系には適しますが、不可逆な拡散、衝撃波、衝突処理へ単に適用することは正当化されません。高次でも無条件安定や同一コストの優位性は示せません。

## シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける — エネルギーと修正Hamiltonian# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/symplectic/#energy-and-a-modified-hamiltonian
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

後退誤差解析は近傍の、一般には形式的な修正Hamiltonianを記述します。滑らかさ、有界軌道、小刻みなどの仮定で、小さな長時間エネルギー誤差を説明できます。すべての軌道・刻みで元のHが厳密不変とはしません。Hairer・Lubich・Wanner（2003）が幾何学的な視点と仮定を論じます。
特別な振動子H=(p²+q²)/2では、kick–drift–kick Verletは、
I_h=\frac12p^2+\frac12\left(1-\frac{h^2}{4}\right)q^2
を丸め誤差まで保存し、H自体は振動します。この不変量から、係数を変えていないHamiltonian流が厳密に数値の時間h写像だとは言えません。|h|<2では有界ですが、それを超えるとシンプレクティックなまま不安定になり得ます。

## シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける — 陰的中点則とRK4の比較# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/symplectic/#implicit-midpoint-and-rk4-as-comparisons
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

陰的中点則は端点方程式を正確に解くとシンプレクティックかつ時間対称です。この2次振動子ではHを丸め誤差まで保存しますが、非2次Hを厳密保存するとは限りません。古典的RK4は4次ですが、一般にはシンプレクティックでも時間対称でもありません。短時間精度の良さだけでは写像の幾何は保証されません。
第2問題はH=p²/2+q²/2+q⁴/4という滑らかな非線形振動子です。中点則の特別な2次エネルギー保存と一般的主張の違いが見えるようになります。

## シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける — 再現可能なノートと検査# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/symplectic/#reproducible-notebook-and-checks
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

from numart.hamiltonian import trajectory, energy, canonical_step, J
t, z = trajectory(h=0.2, steps=1000, method='yoshida4', system='quartic')
print(max(abs((energy(z, 'quartic')-energy(z[0], 'quartic'))/energy(z[0], 'quartic'))))
_, M = canonical_step([0.7, 0.4], 0.2, 'yoshida4', 'quartic', True)
print(M.T @ J @ M - J)
計算データとソース記録は、5手法、2つのHamiltonian、h=0.1、0.2、0.4の30軌道を、(q,p)=(1,0.2)からT=200まで供給します。描画軌道は最大1001標本ですが、最大エネルギー誤差は全積分ステップを使います。位相パッチは(0.7,0.4)中心の正方形へ1ステップ作用させます。標本多角形は図示で、局所欠損は中心の解析的な写像Jacobianを使います。
テストは厳密振動子に対する収束、解析Jacobianと独立差分、両ポテンシャルの正準恒等式、対称法の時間反転、Verletの2次不変量、中点則の2次・非2次エネルギーの違いを確認します。教育用固定刻み例であり、軌道精度や時間コストの順位ではありません。

## シンプレクティック積分：正準写像とエネルギーを分ける — 粒子重力へつなぐ# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/symplectic/#connecting-to-particle-gravity
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

固定刻みと、整合した位置依存ポテンシャルの勾配である力が分割合成の議論を支えます。一般の近似ツリー力、変化する開口判定、場当たり的な格子補間、状態依存の刻み選択が、その証明を自動的に保つわけではありません。力近似と時間積分を合同で検査する必要があります。粒子重力とPoisson解法、重力境界核へ進んでください。

## 時間積分とleapfrog法 — 時間積分とleapfrog法 [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/time-integration/
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

空間再構成と時間積分は独立した選択です。空間離散化後、PDEはODE系dU/dt = L(U)になります。精度、安定性、単調性、散逸、計算量は両者に依存します。時間積分ノートではy′=i y、y(0)=1を使い、時間積分の選択を切り分けます。

## 時間積分とleapfrog法 — ひとつの振動子と12手法# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/time-integration/#twelve-methods-on-one-oscillator
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

厳密解exp(i t)は単位円をたどります。前進Eulerと後退Eulerは1次精度で、この無減衰振動子に対して前者は増幅、後者は減衰します。陽的RK2にはHeun／SSPRK(2,2)、陽的中点、Ralstonがあります。Kutta RK3、SSPRK(3,3)、SSPRK(4,3)は3次、古典的RK4とSSPRK(5,4)は4次です。陰的中点則は2次で、この線形振動子の振幅を保存しますが、位相には誤差があります。RK系譜の章と系譜ノートで段数・次数・SSP、非線形テストを比較できます。
y′=lambda yに対してz=lambda delta tと置くと、1ステップ増幅係数の例は、
R_{\rm FE}=1+z,\quad R_{\rm BE}=\frac1{1-z},\quad
R_{\rm midpoint}=\frac{1+z/2}{1-z/2}.
です。このスカラー線形方程式では、3種のRK2、Kutta RK3／SSPRK(3,3)、古典的RK4のRK係数は、それぞれ2次、3次、4次までの指数関数のTaylor多項式になります。SSPRK(4,3)には4次項z⁴/48、SSPRK(5,4)には5次項もあります。同じスカラー増幅係数でも、非線形RK段階が同じとは限りません。SSP性は空間演算子の前進Euler限界に依存し、無条件安定ではありません。

## 時間積分とleapfrog法 — leapfrog法には2つの根が必要# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/time-integration/#leapfrog-needs-two-roots
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

1階の方程式系を中心差分で進める2ステップ漸化式は、
y^{n+1}=y^{n-1}+2z y^n,\qquad
\xi_\pm=z\pm\sqrt{1+z^2}.
です。zがゼロへ向かうと+1へ近づく根が物理モード、−1へ近づく根がステップごとに交互に変わる計算モードを担います。両方の根と重複度が重要です。z=i sigmaでは、|sigma|<1なら異なる2根の絶対値は1です。|sigma|=1では重根によって線形増大する解があり得るため、一般的な有界性の主張に端点を含めてはいけません。その上では一方の根が等比的に増幅します。
y(0)に加えて開始値が必要です。本実装ではRK4で1ステップ進め、必要に応じてy(1)へ実摂動epsilonを加えます。lambda=0なら、偶数番目の標本は1、奇数番目は1+epsilonとなり、計算モードを直接示せます。ノートの振動子では物理モードも同時に変化します。
Robert–Asselin系などの時間フィルターは、減衰と精度のトレードオフを伴って挙動を変えます。Williams（2009）を参照してください。初版にはフィルターを適用していません。

## 時間積分とleapfrog法 — 粒子leapfrogは別の定式化# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/time-integration/#particle-leapfrog-is-a-different-formulation
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

位置と速度をずらして更新するkick–drift法や、2階の力学系に対する速度Verletも、leapfrogと呼ばれることがあります。変数が異なる時刻位置にあり、シンプレクティックな解釈にはその構造を使います。上のスカラー漸化式は、完全なSPH粒子積分器の実演でも、一般の力学系の長時間エネルギー保存の証明でもありません。

## 時間積分とleapfrog法 — ノートを再現して読む# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/time-integration/#reproduce-and-read-the-notebook
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

from numart.time_integration import linear_trajectory, leapfrog_roots
t, y = linear_trajectory(rate=1j, dt=0.1, steps=200, method='leapfrog')
print(leapfrog_roots(0.1j))
ブラウザーでは、終了時刻20でPython計算した軌道から、12手法、7刻み幅、leapfrog開始摂動3種を選べます。不安定な標本では軸範囲が広がります。陰的求解とRK段数が異なるため、同じ時間区間でも同じ計算量とは限りません。テストでは時間収束次数、leapfrogの根、交互モード、中点則の振幅を確認します。
これらの振動子軌道はスカラー安定性係数を評価し、この線形テスト方程式ではRK段階と代数的に等価です。別の系譜ノートでは完全な非線形段階を評価します。空間安定性実験室、SPH、ALEへ進んでください。

## 時間積分とleapfrog法 — 正準的な力学写像# [ja]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/ja/read/time-integration/#canonical-mechanical-maps
Coverage: reading
Source note: 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。

シンプレクティック積分の章では、調和・4次Hamilton系に対して、力学的なkick–drift–kick Verlet、吉田の4次合成、シンプレクティックEuler、陰的中点則を実装します。写像ノートではRK4と比較し、正準構造と厳密なエネルギー保存を分けます。

## When a moving
biological front stops. — When a moving
biological front stops. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/biophysical-fronts.html
Coverage: reading

Bistability, diffusion and an integral selection condition also organize biological patterns. These primary-source comparisons distinguish shared mathematics from different physical mechanisms.
These are companion references, separate from the thermal-instability paper atlas. No biological simulation or quantitative cross-model reproduction is claimed. Our mathematical comparison uses the KI/ZP saturation benchmark and Elphick, Regev & Shaviv (1992).

## When a moving
biological front stops. — Closest match: wave-pinning in cell polarity. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/biophysical-fronts.html
Coverage: reading

Mori, Jilkine & Edelstein-Keshet (2008), Wave-Pinning and Cell Polarity from a Bistable Reaction-Diffusion System, Biophysical Journal 94, 3684–3697, models slowly diffusing active membrane protein exchanging with a rapidly diffusing inactive pool. Total protein is conserved. An activation front consumes the pool and stops as that pool reaches a critical value.
Equations (10)–(11) and Figure 3 explicitly give a zero-reaction-integral condition, called a Maxwell condition. The near-uniform inactive concentration plays the role of a front-selection parameter; total mass also fixes the eventual front position. In ZP saturation, the selector is pressure and the integral carries the conductivity weight. This is a comparison of selection conditions, not an identification of protein diffusion with thermal conduction.
Biological front: I(b*) = ∫[a− → a+] f(a,b*) da = 0
Planar ZP front: ∫[Tc → Tw] κ(T) Q(T,P_sat) dT = 0
Mori, Jilkine & Edelstein-Keshet (2011), Asymptotic and Bifurcation Analysis of Wave-Pinning in a Reaction-Diffusion Model for Cell Polarization, SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics 71, 1401–1427, analyzes the stationary front, its asymptotic regime and loss through bifurcations. It is the follow-up for evaluating diffusion ratios, total mass and persistence. Author-hosted published paper.

## When a moving
biological front stops. — Closest match: wave-pinning in cell polarity. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/biophysical-fronts.html
Coverage: reading

Possible small benchmark: compute the reaction integral and stationary front first, then let the conserved pool evolve. This would separate a static selector from the mechanism that drives the system toward it. No benchmark has yet been implemented.

## When a moving
biological front stops. — Conserved redistribution and protein-pattern geometry. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/biophysical-fronts.html
Coverage: reading

Brauns, Halatek & Frey (2020), Phase-Space Geometry of Mass-Conserving Reaction-Diffusion Dynamics, Physical Review X 10, 041036, develops local reactive equilibria, diffusion-driven mass redistribution and stationary flux balance for two-component protein-pattern models.
Section III E, equations (16)–(20), selects stationary profiles by zero total reactive turnover. Equation (17) is a reaction-integral balance. Its interpretation as equal geometric areas between a nullcline and a flux-balance line requires additional approximations, stated before equation (19). This is especially relevant to comparing saturation conditions: identify the variable, weight and conserved quantity before drawing equal areas.
The correspondence with thermal fronts is our comparison. These multicomponent dynamics should not automatically be assigned a scalar Ginzburg–Landau free energy. Open-access original paper.

## When a moving
biological front stops. — A related, distinct branch: neural excitability. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/biophysical-fronts.html
Coverage: reading

FitzHugh (1961), Impulses and Physiological States in Theoretical Models of Nerve Membrane, Biophysical Journal 1, 445–466, introduces a two-variable model of excitation and refractoriness, a foundation of the FitzHugh–Nagumo family. Its nullcline geometry and threshold dynamics provide a connection to reduced nonlinear models.
Excitable pulses involve activation followed by recovery. A cubic fast subsystem can resemble a bistable front problem when the slow variable is frozen; a full pulse is not simply a static wall between two thermally stable phases. This is a weaker analogy than wave-pinning for the present saturation-pressure question. The reference was checked at the bibliography and abstract level; its detailed equations and travelling-wave reductions have not been audited here.

## When a moving
biological front stops. — What should be compared? [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/biophysical-fronts.html
Coverage: reading

Retain the number of fields, the conserved quantity, the transport law, the control parameter and the reason a front stops. Protein total-mass conservation and gas mass conservation do not make temperature a conserved order parameter. A geometric resemblance between curves alone does not establish the same instability or the same stationary-front criterion.
The Elphick/Ginzburg–Landau connection supplies the reduced thermal-front functional; Maxwell’s historical construction supplies the thermodynamic comparison. These companion references extend the discussion without treating biological pattern formation as a reproduction of an interstellar calculation.
Sources checked 3 November 2026. Bibliography, reviewed sections and limits / JSON. The four companion papers are linked here; only the explicitly requested Elphick paper has been added to the main thermal-instability catalog.

Historical aside / van der Waals 1873 · Maxwell 1875

## Two phases.
Which area must balance? — Two phases.
Which area must balance? [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/equal-area.html
Coverage: reading

Maxwell’s equal-area construction is a useful companion to ZP saturation. Each selects a coexistence condition through a vanishing integral, with different variables and physical assumptions.

## Two phases.
Which area must balance? — Maxwell’s rule on a van der Waals isotherm. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/equal-area.html
Coverage: reading

For molar volume v, the van der Waals equation is p(T,v) = RT/(v − b) − a/v². The attraction term and excluded volume can give a loop below the critical temperature. At a fixed temperature, Maxwell’s construction selects the liquid–vapour coexistence pressure by balancing signed areas on the pressure–volume diagram:
p(T, v_liquid) = p(T, v_vapour) = p_coexist
∫[v_liquid → v_vapour] [p(T,v) − p_coexist] dv = 0
In modern thermodynamic terms, the two phases share temperature, pressure and chemical potential. The horizontal segment represents changing phase fractions. The mechanically unstable portion of the homogeneous loop is bypassed. Equal areas are coordinate dependent: replacing volume by density requires the inverse-square Jacobian; equal-looking areas on a pressure–density plot do not give the same rule.
Maxwell’s 1875 paper explicitly describes a horizontal line cutting equal areas from an isothermal curve, using a reversible-cycle work argument. The transcription of the original Chemical Society paper preserves that argument. The construction is properly called Maxwell’s equal-area rule, applied here to a van der Waals equation of state.

## Two phases.
Which area must balance? — ZP saturation balances a different integral. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/equal-area.html
Coverage: reading

The cold and warm interstellar phases have different temperatures and are maintained by external heating and radiative cooling. With net volumetric cooling Q = n²Λ − nΓ, a static planar conductive front satisfies:
F = κ(T) dT/dx
F dF/dT = κ(T) Q(T,P)
F(T_cold) = F(T_warm) = 0
∫[T_cold → T_warm] κ(T) Q(T,P_sat) dT = 0
This derivation assumes a static planar front with no mass flux and the specified local cooling law and conductivity. It is an energy-transport selection condition. Thermodynamic liquid–vapour coexistence does not directly supply this pressure. The analogy is cancellation of signed integrals; the ZP condition includes a conductivity weight and integrates over temperature. A Maxwell construction on the interstellar pressure–density equilibrium curve would generally select a different value.
For the corrected KI2002 fit with κ = 2500√T, our computed benchmark gives Psat/kB = 2822.884297 K cm⁻³, with cold and warm endpoints at 54.980188 K and 6417.132178 K. No molecular van der Waals force is added to that gas model.

## Two phases.
Which area must balance? — A scalar Ginzburg–Landau connection. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/equal-area.html
Coverage: reading

A bistable reaction–diffusion equation can have the structure of real, overdamped time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau relaxation. Two stable thermal phases correspond to two potential minima; the unstable equilibrium lies between them. An interface is a domain wall. Equal well depths permit a static planar wall; unequal depths drive its motion.
Elphick, Regev & Shaviv (1992), Dynamics of Fronts in Thermally Bistable Fluids, ApJ 392, 106–117, provide a direct precedent. Their isobaric one-dimensional reduction uses a Lagrangian mass coordinate m. Equations (2.14) and (3.2)–(3.3) have the following dimensionless gradient-flow form:
Z_t = F(Z) + Z^β Z_mm = −Z^β δE/δZ
G(Z,p) = Z^(−β) F(Z,p) = −∂U/∂Z
E[Z] = ∫ [½ (∂Z/∂m)² + U(Z,p)] dm
Z = T^α, β = (α − 1)/α, κ ∝ T^α
For positive temperature the mobility Z^β is positive. With vanishing boundary terms, dE/dt = −∫ Z^(−β) (Z_t)² dm ≤ 0. Their Figure 1 and page 109 explicitly connect equal potential minima with a stationary ZP kink. This source includes fluid motion within the isobaric reduction; it does not reduce the entire compressible problem to an arbitrary scalar equation.
A qualitative illustration from phase.avi. Surrounding axes are cropped; the recording has not been matched to the reduced equation discussed here.

## Two phases.
Which area must balance? — A scalar Ginzburg–Landau connection. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/equal-area.html
Coverage: reading

The computed KI potential wells now compare three pressures with the actual cooling law, explicit normalization and independent quadrature checks.

## Two phases.
Which area must balance? — Recover the ZP condition directly from the static equation. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/equal-area.html
Coverage: reading

The following change of variable is our derivation from the static front equation, rather than a claim that the paper uses the same variable or potential normalization:
θ(T) = ∫ κ(T) dT
θ_xx = Q(T(θ), P)
V(θ;P) = ∫ Q(T(θ), P) dθ
V(θ_warm;P) − V(θ_cold;P)
 = ∫[T_cold → T_warm] κ(T) Q(T,P) dT
At Psat the last integral vanishes: the two minima have equal depths. At a uniform equilibrium, V″ = (∂Q/∂T)P / κ, so the isobarically stable branches are potential minima. For a formal scalar relaxation θ_t = M(θ)[θ_xx − ∂V/∂θ] with M > 0, the same static equation is stationary. This construction establishes the static mathematical correspondence; it does not derive the full time-dependent gas dynamics.
A symmetric quartic double well is a useful cubic-reaction illustration. The KI cooling law is not exactly cubic, and its equal-depth wells need not be mirror symmetric. The functional above is an effective Lyapunov functional of a reduced, externally heated and radiatively cooled system; it is not identified with the equilibrium thermodynamic free energy of the gas. The analogy concerns a real scalar relaxation model, not the full complex order parameter and electromagnetic structure of superconducting Ginzburg–Landau theory. Temperature is not a conserved order parameter, while the underlying gas still conserves mass.

Which area must balance? — The original publications can be traced. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/essays/equal-area.html
Coverage: reading

J. D. van der Waals (1873), Over de continuiteit van den gas- en vloeistoftoestand, doctoral thesis, Leiden, A. W. Sijthoff. Digitized thesis record. Its title and publication details are also identified in Maxwell’s contemporary 1874 review, Nature 10, 477–480.
J. Clerk-Maxwell (1875), On the Dynamical Evidence of the Molecular Constitution of Bodies, Nature 11, 357–359, 4 March 1875; continuation, 374–377, 11 March 1875. The Chemical Society version is Journal of the Chemical Society 28, 493–508; original-text transcription hosted by Le Moyne College.

The 1873 thesis is linked as an original-source destination, but its Dutch text has not been audited here. This aside makes no claim to reconstruct the original diagrams or establish publication priority among all earlier works.

## From historical rates
to the two-phase curve. — The Letter and its detailed companion. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/
Coverage: reading

Field, Goldsmith & Habing (FGH), ApJ 155, L149–L154, presents the equilibrium temperature, pressure, and electron-density curves. Goldsmith, Habing & Field (GHF), ApJ 158, 173–184, explicitly calls that Letter “Paper I” and describes the heating, cooling, and ionization calculation in more detail.
The companion paper supplies the equations and Table 1 used below. Keeping the two sources distinct matters: some printed depletion parameters differ between them.

## From historical rates
to the two-phase curve. — How much ionization energy becomes heat? [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/
Coverage: reading

Derived diagnostics from GHF (1969), equations (25)–(26), printed p. 181. Both curves depend on x = ne/n(H I). Their denominators differ: energy per primary liberated electron is not the same quantity as the fraction of total ionization-plus-excitation losses.SVGPNGHeating data / CSVQ(x) = (1 + 130x)/(1 + 57x)
eh = 9Q eV   ·   f = 0.13Q
The electron fraction changes how energetic electrons share their energy with the gas. Equation (26) gives approximately 9, 13, and 20 eV at x = 10⁻⁴, 10⁻², and 1. The printed fit slightly exceeds 20 eV near x = 1; the code preserves the historical rounded expression.
Equation (23) separately gives Γion/(ζntarget) = 1.4 × 10⁻¹¹Q erg. Here ntarget = n(H I) + n(He I) + n(He II) is the density of primary-ionization targets in equation (20), distinct from the H+He nuclei density n0, and ζ is the cosmic-ray ionization rate. Direct electron heating is another term, Γel = 4.6 × 10⁻¹⁰neζ erg cm⁻³ s⁻¹. It is not added to the plotted energy without specifying the particle populations.
Rounded coefficients in the paper are retained independently: the 0.13 in equation (25) is not forced to equal 1.4/11 from the prefactors of equations (23)–(24).

## From historical rates
to the two-phase curve. — The historical metal cooling coefficients. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/
Coverage: reading

GHF (1969), Table 1, printed p. 179, and equation (16), p. 178. The chosen temperature range evaluates the formulas; it does not independently establish their accuracy over that entire range. Coefficients below 10⁻²⁹ are clipped in the display, while the CSV preserves log₁₀ values.SVGPNGCooling data / CSVTranscribed coefficients / JSONrk(T) = RTmexp(−T*/T)
Λ2 = Σknk(nerek + nHrHk)
These r values have units of erg cm³ s⁻¹: they are energy-loss coefficients, rather than bare excitation probabilities. The relative total cooling contributions require target populations, collider densities, and elemental abundances. A large coefficient alone does not identify the dominant coolant.
Five electron fits and six H-atom fits are transcribed from the table. Missing entries remain unavailable. In particular, a blank for a collider is not treated as a measured zero.

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/cold-branch.html
Coverage: reading

At each trial density and temperature, a monotone bisection solves charge neutrality and the primary ionization/recombination equilibria of H and He. A logarithmic temperature scan identifies sign changes in the net energy loss; bisection then refines each bracket. All sign-changing roots found are retained in the CSV.
ζn(H I) = αB(T)nen(H II)
ne = n(H II) + n(He II) + 2n(He III) + nmetal,e
Γ = 1.4 × 10⁻¹¹Q(x)ζntarget + 4.6 × 10⁻¹⁰neζ
Λmetals + Λrecombination + Λfree-free = Γ
Here ζ = 4 × 10⁻¹⁶ s⁻¹, x = ne/n(H I), Q = (1+130x)/(1+57x), and ntarget = n(H I)+n(He I)+n(He II). This target sum differs from n₀, which counts all H+He nuclei. Heating and cooling are volumetric rates in erg cm⁻³ s⁻¹. The pressure proxy (n₀+ne)T omits trace-element nuclei.
H/He recombination uses the excited-state fits obtained by subtracting Hjellming’s ground-state coefficients from his total coefficients. Recombination kinetic-energy loss follows his energy-weighted definition. The hydrogenic He approximation is a historical approximation whose accuracy at cold-gas temperatures remains to be assessed.

## Find a cold branch.
Keep the assumptions visible. — Read the model before interpreting the curves. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/cold-branch.html
Coverage: reading

Ionization: equal primary rates for H I, He I, and He II; no secondary-electron ionization or thermal collisional ionization.
Cooling: tabulated metal channels, recombination, and free-free emission. Thermal H/He excitation, molecules, grains, and stellar heating are absent. Blank Table 1 channels are omitted inputs, not measured zeros.
Populations: low-density excitation with all C, Si, and Fe singly ionized and O neutral. Each listed transition uses the whole elemental population; no level statistical-equilibrium calculation is included.
Composition: He is 10% of H+He nuclei. Per million H nuclei, C=300, O=670, Si=30, Fe=8, transcribed from Field et al. (1968), Table 1, which cites Allen (1963). We have not directly checked Allen’s book.
Depletion: the FGH Letter divisors are selected explicitly. The different values in the companion GHF paper remain recorded in the source audit.
Search: roots outside 10–2,000 K are outside this calculation. Tangential roots can evade a sign-change scan. Scan refinement checks the reported numerical roots, without proving global completeness.
Curves under these assumptions do not establish the original two-phase pressure interval or a warm branch. Later microphysics will be tracked through Wolfire and GOW references.

The defining result of the FGH model is a pressure curve that turns back on itself. A common pressure can support widely separated equilibrium temperatures and densities. Here the historical ingredients finally enter a coupled cold-to-warm calculation.

The pressure maximum and minimum identify an interval in which a horizontal pressure line intersects multiple equilibria. This is the structure needed for cold and warm phases to coexist in pressure balance. It does not by itself select the pressure of a stationary conductive interface or prove dynamical stability when ionization evolves.
The plotted domain is restricted to 10–12,000 K and 0.01–1,000 cm⁻³. Temperatures without a density bracket are omitted and counted in the report. Temperature parameterization retains folds in T(n), rather than selecting one root and drawing across a missing branch.

The refined normal-abundance warm pressure maximum is 1,516.7 K cm⁻³, compared with the text’s approximately 1,800 K cm⁻³: a −15.7% difference. The corresponding model density is 0.1656 cm⁻³ versus 0.21, and temperature 8,417 K versus 7,800. Near the rapid transition, the largest sampled pressure discrepancy at fixed density is 1.10 dex. and warm phases. — Measure the mismatch, then keep the stopping point explicit. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/two-phase.html

Figure 1 is scored as density at the reference temperature, avoiding arbitrary branch selection near a nearly vertical curve. Figure 2 is scored as pressure or electron density at the reference density, only where there is a unique model temperature root. All candidates would be retained for ambiguous cases; none of these sampled points is unscored. The report gives separate signed and RMS log residuals for each case and quantity; the metrics must not be pooled.

## Connect the cold
and warm phases. — What the coefficient audit resolved. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/two-phase.html
Coverage: reading

GHF Table 1, the equation (13) heating coefficients, and the Field et al. (1968) abundance baseline were visually rechecked. No transcription error was found in these inputs. The earlier Fe cascade discussion also cautions against adding extra lower-level population factors to coefficients that describe total excitation losses.
At the text’s n = 0.21 cm⁻³, T = 7,800 K point, the implemented cooling is 1.171 times the heating. Si II supplies about 31.4% of model cooling and the O I 22,500-K term about 18.0%. The downloadable report separates every heating and cooling contribution.
One-term sensitivity probes do not identify a correction: halving or doubling thermal Lyman-alpha cooling shifts the warm pressure maximum by only about +1.6% or −1.9%; applying the printed GHF 2/3 recombination-energy factor shifts it by less than 1%. These are diagnostics, not recovered cross sections, uncertainty bounds, or alternative fits to the original curve.
Stopping note: the original excitation fit, thermal He processes, recombination convention, and exact historical implementation remain unresolved. The prototype and measured discrepancies are preserved. We will resume historical coefficient recovery if a missing fit, original code, or other discriminating source becomes available.

## Connect the cold
and warm phases. — What changed from the reduced cold branch? [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/two-phase.html
Coverage: reading

The solver now includes cosmic-ray production and removal of 20-eV superthermal electrons, secondary hydrogen ionization, thermal hydrogen excitation and ionization, and direct electron heating. These interact with H/He recombination, charge neutrality, historical metal cooling, and free-free emission.
ζ[n(H I) + n(He I) + n(He II)]
= nfast[n(H I)(q′ion + q′ex) + neq′ee]
Γindirect = nfast[3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ n(H I) + 4.1 × 10⁻¹⁷ ne]
These follow GHF equations (13) and (20). Heating is evaluated directly from the superthermal population, with ζ = 4 × 10⁻¹⁶ s⁻¹. The closure uses the printed H/He charge balance, without added metal-donor electrons. The earlier primary-only cold-branch calculation remains available to inspect that approximation separately.

## Connect the cold
and warm phases. — The atomic-data gap is explicit. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/two-phase.html
Coverage: reading

GHF p. 178 prints the hydrogen ionization triangle: threshold 13.6 eV, peak cross section 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁶ cm² at 50 eV, and zero at 300 eV. Its Maxwellian average is integrated analytically and checked against independent numerical quadrature.
The same page does not print the complete Lyman-alpha fit, referring instead to Fite, Stebbings & Brackmann (1959) and Goldsmith’s Berkeley thesis (1969). We infer the excitation cross section at 20 eV from rounded equations (12)–(13), after subtracting the explicit ionization contribution. A linear rise from the 10.2-eV threshold is an assumption; it has not been validated against those data.
Two alternative tails beyond 20 eV change the calculated density at fixed temperature by at most about 0.13% over the sampled roots. That small sensitivity does not validate the assumed threshold slope or its normalization. The separate recombination-energy convention test changes density by at most about 0.65%.
Thermal He excitation and ionization are omitted. He I recombination uses the hydrogen approximation; metal cooling uses a low-density sum without level statistical equilibrium. The full list is in the configuration and limitations. The figure uses historical inputs with these declared approximations; it does not substitute a modern KI or Wolfire cooling fit.

## Connect the cold
and warm phases. — A bounded ZP saturation search. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/fgh-1969/two-phase.html

This supplementary calculation uses the existing approximate FGH/GHF model with instantaneous ionization equilibrium, P/kB = (n0 + ne)T, and an explicitly assumed neutral-gas conductivity κ = 2500√T. It is not a recovery of historical FGH saturation values. The depleted warm branches remain model extensions beyond the source’s cold-side depletion prescription.
For normal abundances, 13 sampled pressures between 608.68 and 1471.19 K cm⁻³ have three equilibrium roots within 10–12,000 K, but the conductivity-weighted integral remains positive (normalized range 0.196–0.997). ## How thermal conduction
sets a small-scale limit. — Long wavelengths [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/
Coverage: reading

For this choice of α, the gas is stable to an isochoric perturbation but unstable to isobaric condensation. At small wavenumber, the finite sound speed limits the growth; the normalized rate tends to zero linearly with wavenumber.

## How thermal conduction
sets a small-scale limit. — Short wavelengths [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/
Coverage: reading

Without conduction, the rate approaches 0.3. With conduction, temperature perturbations are smoothed on small scales. Each conducting curve reaches a finite cutoff beyond which the linear system is stable.

## How thermal conduction
sets a small-scale limit. — One cubic, one growing root. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/
Coverage: reading

Field writes perturbations as exp(nt + i k·r): positive real n means growth. Using equations (27) and (38), define q = k/kρ, x = n/(kρc), α = kT/kρ, and β = kρ/kK. Here c is the adiabatic sound speed and the three characteristic wavenumbers are defined by equation (16).
x³ + (α + βq²)x² + q²x + q²(α − 1 + βq²)/γ = 0
Equation (39), regrouped as a cubic in x. The heat-loss function is energy losses minus gains per unit mass per unit time. β = 0 is the zero-conductivity limit. These normalizations assume kρ > 0, as in Figure 2.
For these parameters the polynomial is strictly increasing for nonnegative x. Within the unstable band it has exactly one positive root, which the code finds by bisection. At q = 0 it uses the limiting value x = 0.
For β > 0, the neutral cutoff is qc = √[(1 − α)/β]: approximately 7.0711, 2.2361, and 0.7071 for β = 0.01, 0.1, and 1. The first lies just beyond the plotted range, as in the original figure. Stable-domain growth values are left blank in the CSV.

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-1.html
Coverage: reading

The stability domains place condensation and acoustic growth in a common plane. Two straight neutral lines count growing roots; two hatched regions distinguish oscillation from non-oscillatory evolution.

## A map of growing modes. — The domains, recomputed. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-1.html

Field (1965), Figure 1, printed p. 536; γ = 5/3. Color indicates the number of roots with positive real part, counted with multiplicity. Hatching means three real distinct roots. Neutral lines are treated separately. The circular annotation guide in the original is omitted because it is not a stability boundary.SVG figurePNG figureDomain grid / CSVConductive paths / CSVValidation / JSON

## A map of growing modes. — Conduction is already on the horizontal axis. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-1.html
Coverage: reading

Equation (17) defines y = n/(kc), σρ = kρ/k, and σT′ = kT/k + k/kK. The horizontal coordinate includes the positive thermal-conduction contribution. Both coordinates and y are dimensionless; c is the adiabatic sound speed.
y³ + σT′y² + y + (σT′ − σρ)/γ = 0
Equation (18). This normalization uses kc; Figures 2 and 3 instead use kρc.

## A map of growing modes. — The neutral lines [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-1.html
Coverage: reading

The solid line σρ = σT′ has a zero root and is the isobaric neutral line. The dashed line σρ = −(γ − 1)σT′ has purely imaginary roots and is the isentropic neutral line.

## A map of growing modes. — The hatched thorns [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-1.html
Coverage: reading

The discriminant boundary changes the character of the roots. Inside the hatching, all three roots are real and distinct. Outside, there is one real root and a complex conjugate pair. The hatching is not an additional instability threshold.

## A map of growing modes. — The hatched thorns [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-1.html
Coverage: reading

A growing root means Re(y) > 0. A complex conjugate pair with positive real part counts as two growing roots. Away from neutral lines, the count is:
N = 1[σρ > σT′]
+ 2[σρ < −(γ − 1)σT′]
Here 1[condition] is 1 when the condition is true, otherwise 0. On neutral lines the CSV leaves N blank, so zero-real-part roots are not classified by an off-boundary rule.

## A map of growing modes. — Keep Field’s sign convention. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-1.html
Coverage: reading

Write t = σT′ and r = σρ. Field’s equation (19) defines:
D = [(t − r)/γ − t/3 + 2t³/27]²/4
+ [1 − t²/3]³/27
For this definition, D < 0 gives three real roots, while D > 0 gives a complex pair. The conventional cubic discriminant is −108D, with the opposite sign. Equation (20) supplies the thorn boundaries; their tips are triple roots at t = ±√3, r = (1 − γ/9)t.

## A map of growing modes. — Follow a path into Figures 2 and 3. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-1.html
Coverage: reading

With q = k/kρ > 0, equation (28) gives r = 1/q and t = α/q + βq = αr + β/r. The green paths use α = 1/2, as in Figure 2; the brown paths use α = −2, as in Figure 3. Each family has β = 0.01, 0.1, 1, with dotted zero-conduction reference rays.
Increasing wavenumber moves toward smaller positive r. Conduction shifts the path to the right, where it can cross the neutral lines. The growth-rate normalization converts as x = qy. The validation checks this mapping using all three roots along each conducting path.
A path can cross the wave neutral line while condensation is still unstable. The map counts all growing roots; the wave cutoff in Figure 3 concerns only the acoustic pair.

## When sound waves grow. — When sound waves grow. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-3.html
Coverage: reading

An oscillation can grow while it travels. Figure 3 follows the real part of the acoustic wave pair in Field’s dispersion relation, with α = −2.
Recomputed and numerically validated. The calculation selects the complex wave pair explicitly: the fastest-growing root belongs to a different mode. No digitized pointwise comparison with the printed curves has been performed.

## When sound waves grow. — The wave mode, recomputed. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-3.html
Coverage: reading

Field (1965), Figure 3, printed p. 540. α = −2, γ = 5/3; β = 0, 0.01, 0.1, 1. Both axes are dimensionless. Growing branches and neutral endpoints are shown; the CSV also includes signed damping rates and frequencies.SVG figurePNG figureGrowth & frequency / CSVValidation / JSON

## When sound waves grow. — The real part: growth [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-3.html
Coverage: reading

Write x = ξ + iη, with time normalized by kρc. The real part ξ sets the exponential growth or decay of the disturbance. Positive ξ is an oscillatory instability, also called overstability.

## When sound waves grow. — The imaginary part: frequency [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-3.html
Coverage: reading

The two conjugate roots have opposite frequencies and equal growth rates. The code keeps the positive-frequency member, η > 0. The figure plots ξ; the CSV retains both ξ and η.

## When sound waves grow. — The imaginary part: frequency [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-3.html
Coverage: reading

At long wavelengths, Re(x) tends to zero quadratically with q = k/kρ. Without conduction it approaches 0.1 at short wavelengths. Increasing conduction reduces growth and introduces a finite wave cutoff.

## When sound waves grow. — The growing wave is not the fastest root. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-3.html
Coverage: reading

As in Figure 2, define x = n/(kρc), q = k/kρ, α = kT/kρ, β = kρ/kK, and s = α + βq². The same dispersion relation applies:
x³ + sx² + q²x + q²(s − 1)/γ = 0
At q = 0, the wave pair tends to x = 0, whereas the condensation root tends to −α = 2. Selecting the root with the largest real part would draw the condensation mode instead of Figure 3. The script identifies the unique root with positive imaginary part and fails if no unique wave pair exists.
Equation (40) provides a separate check on ξ = Re(x):
ξ³ + sξ² + (s² + q²)ξ/4
+ q²[(1 − 1/γ)s + 1/γ]/8 = 0

## When sound waves grow. — A damped wave can coexist with condensation. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-3.html
Coverage: reading

The wave cutoff follows equation (26): qc = √[(−α − 1/(γ − 1))/β] = √(0.5/β). For β = 0.01, 0.1, and 1 this is approximately 7.0711, 2.2361, and 0.7071. The first is just outside the plotted interval.
At the cutoff, s = −1.5 and the cubic factors as (x + s)(x² + q²). The wave roots are purely imaginary, x = ±iq, but the condensation root remains x = 1.5.
The wave mode is damped above its cutoff. This does not imply stability of the whole gas: for these parameters the condensation mode remains unstable until a higher wavenumber.

## When sound waves grow. — Follow the wave all the way to damping. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/field-1965/figure-3.html
Coverage: reading

Compare both members of the complex pair against the eigenvalues of the linearized fluid equations.
Check the complex residual of equation (39) and the real-part residual of equation (40).
Check Re(x)/q² → 0.025 and Im(x)/q → √0.9 at long wavelengths.
For zero conduction, check Re(x) → 0.1 and Im(x)/q → 1 at short wavelengths.
Check zero growth, frequency η = q, and the change to damping at each conductive wave cutoff.
Confirm that the selector excludes the faster condensation root and that condensation can still grow when the waves are damped.
All 24 checks passed in the recorded run. The script stops on a validation failure. Measured errors and tolerances are available in the validation report.
The plotted geometry has been inspected against the scan, but no error relative to digitized original curves is claimed. Peaks are sampled maxima. The β = 0 endpoint at q = 7 is not a physical finite-wavenumber maximum. Magnetic fields, gravity, and nonlinear evolution are outside this calculation.

## An archive in motion. — What these recordings can tell us. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/gallery/
Coverage: reading

They are effective visual demonstrations at compact gallery sizes. Their native resolutions are 500–800 pixels wide and their cadences are 3–10 fps. Fine textures can look grainy, and low-frame-rate motion is visibly stepped. They are suitable as historical exhibits; they are not high-resolution, full-screen source material.
The 3D recordings carry the embedded credit “Koyama & Inutsuka 2002”. This identifies the caption on the recording; it does not establish a match to a specific paper figure, simulation dimensionality in that paper, or verified numerical parameters. The 2D titles here describe the visible panels and evolution. A number in a filename is not treated as a confirmed computational mesh size.
The gallery was curated from 87 video files, representing 55 byte-distinct recordings after SHA-256 deduplication. Astronomy candidates were visually inspected at several times. The eight selected originals and their MP4 derivatives were decoded completely; dimensions and frame counts were checked. These are technical media checks, not numerical or physical validation of the simulations.

A pressure and a mass flux can select very different connections between cold and warm gas. We solve the steady front equations behind the paper’s classification diagrams, starting from the cold neutral medium.
This is a computed subset prepared for technical review, not a completed reproduction of every published region or auxiliary curve. Nine published example classifications agree. ## Classify the interface
by following its trajectory. — Toward Figure 5: pressure and condensation flux. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/iwasaki-2012/
Coverage: reading

29 pressure samples × 45 flux samples. Each cell is computed from the printed model. The white dashed curve is the condensation ZP separatrix, found by matching phase integrations from the cold and warm equilibria. Gray inputs lack the outgoing CNM saddle on the implemented density branch. White is unresolved. The source jcrit overlay remains to be audited.PNGSVGAll decisions / CSVComputed boundaries / CSV
C–U–o approaches unstable gas with a temperature overshoot; C–U approaches it monotonically. C–c reaches the critical point, while C–C connects cold equilibria. A local node at the unstable equilibrium is insufficient to establish C–U: the paper explicitly notes that the global trajectory can still overshoot.
The condensation flux is plotted as −j divided by mH × (1 cm⁻³) × (1 km s⁻¹). Positive plotted values therefore mean negative physical j. The physical mass flux has units g cm⁻² s⁻¹; the density unit implicit in the source’s compact axis label is explicit here.

## Classify the interface
by following its trajectory. — Check the equilibrium landmarks first. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/iwasaki-2012/
Coverage: reading

Equations (5)–(7) set the thermal equilibrium curve. Equation (16), the conductivity-weighted net-loss integral, selects the saturation pressure.Equilibrium data / CSVSVG
The printed cooling fit gives Pmin/kB = 1,597.45, Pmax/kB = 5,007.00, and Psat/kB = 2,822.88 K cm⁻³. The source quotes 1596 in the text / 1598 in Figure 1, 5012, and 2823. These small differences are retained.
At Pc/kB = 3,000 K cm⁻³, the matched condensation ZP flux is −j = 0.00315993 in the plotted normalization, close to the quoted 0.0032. The calculation preserves constant mass and momentum flux and uses the full plus-density branch of equation (11), rather than imposing constant pressure throughout the front.

## Classify the interface
by following its trajectory. — What is being solved? [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/iwasaki-2012/
Coverage: reading

ρv = j   ·   ρv² + P = M
ρ(T) = [M + √(M²−4ℛj²T)]/(2ℛT)
d(F²)/dT = ℛj[(γ+1)/(γ−1)+M/√(M²−4ℛj²T)]F + 2κρℒ
Here dθ = κdT and F = dθ/dx = κdT/dx. The physical conductive heat flux is −F. The CNM boundary is a thermal equilibrium with F = 0, approached along its outgoing saddle eigenvector. The source heating/cooling fit, pure atomic hydrogen, γ = 5/3, and κ = 2500√T are used.
For node-like targets, the solver follows log(F) and refines the remaining temperature distance. A captured trajectory has F proportional to that distance; a crossing retains finite F. Two consecutive refinements must agree. Ambiguous cases remain white. Grid boundaries have not been digitized against the published figure.

## Classify the interface
by following its trajectory. — Two implementation questions to discuss with the authors. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/iwasaki-2012/
Coverage: reading

Continuation of the CNM boundary: at large imposed flux, the implemented plus-density branch can lose its outgoing CNM saddle. How should the boundary or branch be continued to recover the rest of the published C–C coverage?
The reference state for jcrit: what temperature interval and loss normalization were used to choose Tm in section 4.1.2? The prototype does not infer an unprinted selection, so it omits that overlay.
These are questions about the present implementation and interpretation. They are not assertions of errors in the paper. A useful first review package is this page, the nine example checks, the source audit, and the two grid CSVs.
The first technical milestone is agreement on these model choices. Quantitative boundary comparisons, finer sampling, and broader continuation can then follow. The front lineage provides the context connecting Zel’dovich–Pikel’ner, Penston–Brown, Nagashima, and later front studies.

## One cooling law.
Two stable phases. — One cooling law.
Two stable phases. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/ki-2002/
Coverage: reading

Balance heating and cooling, follow the stable and unstable branches, and locate the pressure that supports a static planar conductive front.
A new diagnostic of the corrected model, with numerical validation. This does not reproduce the original two-dimensional simulation or claim to digitize an equilibrium figure from the 2002 paper. The same cooling law underlies our Iwasaki & Inutsuka (2012) front prototype.

## One cooling law.
Two stable phases. — Temperature, density and pressure. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/ki-2002/
Coverage: reading

Pure atomic H: n = ρ/mH and P/kB = nT. The corrected fit gives isobaric instability between 184.000 and 5039.419 K, corresponding to densities between 0.993567 and 8.681810 cm⁻³. The endpoints are marginal. Dots mark the cold, intermediate and warm intersections at the ZP saturation pressure.PNGSVGEquilibria / CSV
With net volumetric cooling Q = n²Λ − nΓ, thermal equilibrium gives n = Γ/Λ(T) and P/kB = TΓ/Λ(T). Here Γ = 2 × 10⁻²⁶ erg per H atom per second; Λ is in erg cm³ s⁻¹. Let β = d ln Λ / d ln T. At equilibrium, (∂Q/∂T)P = nΓ(β − 1)/T. The local isobaric thermal mode is stable for β > 1 and unstable for β < 1.
These branch labels omit the wavelength dependence of conduction, which stabilizes sufficiently small scales. The isochoric derivative is positive throughout the displayed interval. The plotted 10–10,000 K range is a diagnostic choice, not a claim that a temperature-only fit describes all chemistry or ionization there.
The turning pressures are Pmin/kB = 1597.453 and Pmax/kB = 5007.000 K cm⁻³. Two stable equilibria share a pressure between these limits; a static conductive front imposes an additional condition.

## One cooling law.
Two stable phases. — ZP saturation and its equilibrium points. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/ki-2002/
Coverage: reading

Psat/kB = 2822.884297 K cm⁻³. For a planar, static front with zero conductive flux at each end, integrate d(κ dT/dx)/dx = Q to obtain ∫TcTw κ(T) Q(T,P) dT = 0. We use κ = 2500√T erg cm⁻¹ K⁻¹ s⁻¹. An unweighted equal-area construction on the pressure–density plot would give a different condition.

## One cooling law.
Two stable phases. — Warm endpoint [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/ki-2002/
Coverage: reading

The intermediate point is the third intersection of the common-pressure line with the equilibrium curve. It is not a third asymptotic endpoint of this cold-to-warm static front. Uniform equilibria have no temperature gradient; conduction selects the connecting front without moving the equilibrium curve.
Pressure and all three points / CSVPrecision and checks / JSONCross-model landmark registry / JSON
Iwasaki & Inutsuka (2012), equations (4)–(7), use the same pure-H pressure convention, corrected rates and conductivity. Our two implementations agree on Psat to better than 10⁻¹⁰ relative precision. The paper prints Psat/kB = 2823, Pmax/kB = 5012, and Pmin/kB = 1596 in the text or 1598 in Figure 1. We retain these small numerical differences instead of fitting coefficients to the labels. A nonzero mass flux changes the front problem; uniform thermal equilibrium alone does not determine the pressure–mass-flux classification.
For the FGH/GHF prototype, the bounded saturation search is recorded separately. Its density includes H and He nuclei plus electrons in the pressure. Its unresolved historical coefficients prevent assigning a historical FGH saturation value.

## One cooling law.
Two stable phases. — Pressure tilts the two thermal wells. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/ki-2002/
Coverage: reading

Compare P/Psat = 0.9, 1 and 1.1 using the same corrected cooling law, pure-H density convention and Parker conductivity as the equilibrium benchmark. This is a new static-front diagnostic of the model, not an original-paper figure reproduction.
The cold minimum sets V = 0 separately at each pressure; all curves share one vertical scale, the intermediate barrier at saturation. Blue marks cold equilibria, orange intermediate equilibria, and green warm equilibria. The wide figure compares logarithmic temperature (top) with the natural conduction coordinate (bottom). On narrow screens the temperature panels are stacked vertically. The minima are strongly asymmetric in the conduction coordinate.

## One cooling law.
Two stable phases. — The coordinate and potential have explicit definitions. [en]

Source: https://koyamahr.github.io/the-art-of-thermal-instability/ki-2002/
Coverage: reading

Q(T,P) = n²Λ(T) − nΓ, n = (P/kB)/T
κ(T) = 2500 √T
θ(T) = ∫κ(T) dT = (5000/3) T^(3/2)
V(θ(T),P) = ∫[Tcold(P) → T] κ(s) Q(s,P) ds
∂V/∂θ = Q
θ has units erg cm⁻¹ s⁻¹ and V has units erg² cm⁻⁴ s⁻², the square of an energy flux. V is an effective static-front potential, not the thermodynamic free energy of the gas. Its additive constant is arbitrary; choosing Vcold = 0 makes the difference between the two minima directly visible. The shared scale is Vbarrier,sat = 3.425672655 × 10⁻¹⁸ erg² cm⁻⁴ s⁻².
At a thermal equilibrium, ∂²V/∂θ² = (∂Q/∂T)P / κ. Thus the two isobarically stable equilibria are minima and the unstable intersection is a maximum. A monotonic relabeling from θ to log T preserves these extrema and their depths; it changes the apparent shape and width of the wells.
